title: Split hero with text and image side by side
when: The user wants a hero section with the message on one side and an image, illustration or short form on the other.
prompt:
Goal: A hero with headline, line and action beside a visual on wide screens, stacking text first on phones.
Steps:
1. Markup: a section with a text block (h1, one paragraph, a primary and a secondary link) then a figure or img.
2. Layout: grid with gap var(--space-6), one column by default, grid-template-columns: 1.1fr 1fr and align-items: center from about 54em.
3. Keep text first in the source; to show the image on the left, move it with grid-column, not by DOM order.
4. Size the h1 with clamp(2rem, 1.2rem + 3vw, 3.5rem) and cap the paragraph at 45ch.
5. Give the img width, height, aspect-ratio with object-fit: cover, and fetchpriority="high".
6. Keep padding modest, clamp(2rem, 6vw, 6rem), so the action shows on a 375 by 667 screen.
Quality bar:
- Headline and button fit the first phone screen.
- The image never squashes.
- Text and visual balance in weight.
Pitfalls:
- Text over a busy photo with no overlay.
- Image first on phones, pushing the message down.
- min-height: 100vh heroes that waste the screen.
Verify:
- [ ] One h1 in the hero.
- [ ] Two columns in a media query.
- [ ] The img has alt, width and height.
- [ ] The primary action is a real link.
Output: The hero section in index.html and its rules in style.css.

examples.input: hero com texto de um lado e foto do produto do outro
examples.output: grid 1.1fr 1fr from 54em, h1 with clamp, photo 4:3 with fetchpriority high
